messages:
oncall-bot: ACTION REQUIRED - Significant p99 latency spike detected on inference-path (streaming tails showing stalls). Paging current on-call: @maria g (oncall). Auto-alert: increased 429s from control-plane config fetch and auth service. Correlation ID: cid=0a1b2c3d.

maria g (oncall): I'm on it. initial read: p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.1s; p99 from ~900ms to ~6.8s in last 5m. Streaming clients reporting stalls ~20-40s. Are we seeing backend 5xx/429s?

sam v (infra): yes seeing elevated 429s from config-store and auth-proxy around 23:11 UTC. Rate-limiter counters spiked. top-line: config-fetch rps unchanged but error-rate up.

ashwin r (sre): adding logs: `kubectl logs -n controlplane config-fetcher-7b9c -c fetcher | tail -n 200` shows repeated `HTTP 429 /config?client=svc-token` and `backpressure: token bucket depleted`.

kevin t (db): DB metrics show short bursts on the featureflag read replica causing increased read latency (p99 reads 120ms -> 650ms). Not enough to explain multi-second inference p99 but will cascade with retries.

adrian m (mlops): inference runtime sees KV cache misses increase 3x concurrently with config fetch failures. We rely on config for routing/quantization decisions; fallback path triggers additional calls -> blowup.

maria g (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) enable conservative caching for config (TTL -> 5m) 2) route reads to standby region for non-critical flags 3) throttle internal retries. Who can flip caching?

sam v (infra): I can toggle config cache policy via the control plane. Running: `POST /admin/flags/cache?ttl=300` now (will push to all nodes). Pushing in 10s.

sam v (infra): done. config cache TTL set to 300s across control-plane. watch for reduced fetch rate.

ashwin r (sre): I'm temporarily lowering retry backoff on fetcher from exponential(100ms..5s) to fixed 500ms and capping max retries to 2 to avoid retry storms. Applying canary now.

kevin t (db): I increased read replica pool by +2 nodes in prod-read-replica autoscaling group (manual) — should reduce read p99 by spreading load. Takes ~45s to warm.

liz p (product): any customer impact? Sharon from CS is on this thread. Sharon, can you summarize open customer reports?

sharon (cs): We have ~7 customer tickets flagged as intermittent streaming stalls and one customer reported a degraded SLA on a critical job that hit p99s ~8s. They've been triaged as P2/P1 depending on SLA. Not spreading widely yet.

maria g (oncall): good. Next: fallback routing. If control-plane still rate-limiting, we should route inference calls to the read-only cached config mode (best-effort) and enable stateless auth fallback for tokens within grace period. Adrian, can you change serving policy?

adrian m (mlops): yes. Preparing rollout: `curl -XPOST https://console.api/redwood/rollouts -d '{"route":"inference*","policy":"cached-config-fallback"}'` will apply. Pushing to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30s intervals. Starting now.

adrian m (mlops): rollout at 10% -> 50% (30s). Monitoring streaming tail latency.

oncall-bot: METRIC UPDATE: inference-path.p95=1.08s p99=5.9s (5m window) streaming.stalls=78 events/min config-fetch.429=23% auth.429=16%

maria g (oncall): after TTL and rollout, I see p95 trending down to ~640ms, p99 down to ~2.4s. streaming stalls decreased to ~22 events/min. still above baseline.

kevin t (db): read replica nodes are in; DB p99 read latency dropping to ~180ms. That should help further.

ashwin r (sre): logs show client-side retries reduced by ~65% post-backoff change. No additional 5xx from config-store. Good.

liz p (product): any config flags we should roll back? We had a recent feature-flag push for `ff/new-routing` that increased control-plane reads for per-request decisions. Consider rolling it back to reduce pressure.

maria g (oncall): agree — rolling back `ff/new-routing` for now. Sam, can you flip it?

sam v (infra): rolling back flag via admin: `POST /admin/featureflags/ff:new-routing/false` -> done. Propagation across nodes ~5-8s.

oncall-bot: NOTE: automatic incident escalation threshold cleared? current p99=1.9s, threshold=3s. Notifying oncall that active mitigations reduced overload.

sharon (cs): updated affected customers: one P1 alerted with temporary SLA breach; provided mitigation summary and ETA for full restoration. Customers asked for sticky details — sending follow-up email after final state.

maria g (oncall): action items before closing: 1) keep TTL 5m for 30m then assess 2) schedule postmortem to analyze why `ff/new-routing` caused disproportionate config reads + consider guardrails 3) create runbook step for aggressive retry capping during control-plane rate spikes 4) tune rate-limiter burst window for control-plane. Assign owners?

ashwin r (sre): I'll take runbook and postmortem ownership.

kevin t (db): I'll investigate read replica autoscaling threshold and add a temporary policy to scale earlier on read latency increases.

adrian m (mlops): I'll follow up on the rollout telemetry and ensure cached-config-fallback preserves safety properties (model selection, quantization).

liz p (product): I'll coordinate product-level mitigation and requirements to avoid per-request feature flag hell.

maria g (oncall): timeline: targeting full return to baseline p95<300ms p99<1s within 30min. Current status at 23:19 UTC: p95=340ms p99=980ms streaming.stalls ~4 events/min. I'll keep thread open for 45min for monitoring.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT: status=mitigated -> monitors warming. Incident owner: maria g (oncall).

sharon (cs): I pushed an interim status update to affected customers. Will send final note once we hit stable baseline. :thumbsup:

maria g (oncall): thanks everyone. if anything regresses, ping here and we'll re-open. closing incident thread in 45m if stable.
